scenarios.name: ci-dag-from-scratch
scenarios.description: User builds a CI pipeline DAG from scratch: lint, build, test, deploy — defining each node, wiring dependencies, running, fixing failures

turns.speak: create a new DAG called ci-pipeline with three nodes: lint, build, and test, in that order
for lint, use cargo clippy. for build, use cargo build. for test, use cargo test.
add a deploy node after test that echoes deploying to staging
now run the full DAG and tell me each node's result as it finishes
something failed in the build node, show me the node log
fix the build error, then restart the DAG from the build node onward

scenarios.name: retry-with-backoff
scenarios.description: User defines a flaky deployment flow with retry logic, observes failures, tunes retry parameters

turns.speak: create a DAG called deploy that uploads to the server, then verifies the upload, then restarts the service
make the upload step retry up to three times with a five second delay between attempts
run it and tell me how many attempts the upload took
it took all three attempts, increase the retry count to five and use exponential backoff
run it again and compare the timing to the previous run

scenarios.name: param-passing-pipeline
scenarios.description: User builds a DAG where each node consumes output from the previous — git branch → checkout → build → tag

turns.speak: create a DAG called release where the first node gets the current git branch name
the second node should take the branch name from the first node and run git checkout on it
add a third node that builds the project, and a fourth node that creates a git tag with the version from the branch name
run the DAG and show me the output of each node as it passes data to the next
the tag creation should only run if the build succeeds, make that a conditional dependency

scenarios.name: http-api-node
scenarios.description: User adds an HTTP API call as a DAG node — posts build status to Slack, reads response, branches on result

turns.speak: add an HTTP node to the ci-pipeline DAG that posts the build status to a webhook URL
the webhook URL is http colon slash slash localhost colon 8080 slash webhook and it should send a JSON body with the status and the branch name
make the HTTP node run in parallel with the deploy node, they don't depend on each other
if the HTTP call fails, the DAG should continue — don't block on notification failures
run the full DAG and tell me whether both the deploy and the notification completed

scenarios.name: tts-feedback-loop
scenarios.description: User runs a long DAG — each node completion is spoken back via TTS so the user can monitor progress hands-free

turns.speak: run the full ci-pipeline DAG and speak each node's result as it finishes
the test node failed, what was the failure message
skip the test node for now and continue from build to deploy
now go back and run just the test node with verbose output, speak the summary

scenarios.name: abort-and-cleanup
scenarios.description: User aborts a running DAG mid-execution, inspects partial state, cleans up, restarts from scratch

turns.speak: start the full deployment DAG
wait, stop it immediately, I realized the config is wrong
show me which nodes already ran and what state they left behind
clean up any partial state from the aborted run
now update the deploy node to use the staging environment and restart from the beginning

scenarios.name: parallel-fanout
scenarios.description: User builds a fan-out DAG: one node splits into three parallel tasks, then a gather node collects results

turns.speak: create a DAG called benchmark that runs three benchmarks in parallel: whisper, moonshine, and parakeet
each benchmark node should just run the corresponding cargo bench command
add a gather node that waits for all three benchmarks and prints a comparison table
run it and tell me which engine was fastest and by how much

scenarios.name: dag-persistence-and-replay
scenarios.description: User saves a DAG definition, modifies it later, and replays from a checkpoint

turns.speak: save the ci-pipeline DAG to a file so I can reuse it later
now load the ci-pipeline DAG and add a notification node before the deploy step
run it — if the lint and build nodes passed last time, skip them and start from test
save the updated DAG with a new name ci-pipeline-with-notify
